note: Reconstructed from this session's own fix record after a context compaction discarded the doubt-reviewer subagent's verbatim reply text. Not a fabricated quote -- the two doubts below are traceable to the exact code changes that resolved them (codex-task-watcher.ts + codex-task-watcher.test.ts).

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The oracle-done classify() branch in codex-task-watcher.ts correctly finalizes a completed Codex task.
doubts.disproof_attempt: It patches only { state: "done" }, never syncing boardColumn -- CLAUDE.md rule 23 requires a done transition to also sync boardColumn (the /close route already does this). A task the operator had dragged to a non-Done column stayed stranded there once auto-completed, locked with no visible reason since no Resume/Launch CTA reads boardColumn once state is done.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: patch { state: "done", boardColumn: "done" } together, mirroring lifecycle.ts's /close fix

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The launch_confirmation_failed notice set in checkTask() only ever appears while genuinely needed.
doubts.disproof_attempt: Once set while a task sat in awaiting_external_start past the launch-confirm window, nothing cleared it if the task later moved on and started producing output normally -- only a full "done" transition clears the notices map. An otherwise-healthy run that simply started slowly kept a stale "may not have started correctly" banner in the Inbox indefinitely.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: clear a stale launch_confirmation_failed notice as soon as state is observed to have left awaiting_external_start

disposed_no_fix.note: execFile's timeout only SIGTERMs the immediate uv child; on Windows an already-forked Python grandchild is not reaped, and this runs every 60s tick per stalled task. Accepted -- tick()'s per-task sequential await bounds this to at most one in-flight oracle call at a time, so the exposure is more repeats of an existing, already-accepted risk pattern (triage-cli-runner.ts precedent), not a new class of leak. Documented in the module header.

HEAD_BYTES=4096 read cap: if a future session_meta line ever exceeds it, discovery fails identically and permanently for that task on every later tick. Accepted -- the verified real session_meta line is compact and 4KB is a generous margin; documented above HEAD_BYTES with a revisit note (retry-on-parse-failure) if a future Codex CLI version grows this payload.
